note: Audited per-team offseason state derived from the reconciled feed — how each team's July actually happened, which the raw cap sheet can't show. Five audit agents replayed every feed signing against the exception system; rationale fields are the per-signing audit trail. Ambiguous forced-renounce sets follow a prefer-largest-holds rule and carry confidence: medium.

ATL.rationale: Jock Landale 1y/$14.0M (y1 14,000,000, prior ATL): 2025-26 salary was the minimum ($2,296,274), so his Non-Bird ceiling (120%) is ~$2.76M and even the Early-Bird 105%-of-average prong (~$13.86M) falls short of $14M — the Bird family cannot produce this deal. Confirmed by in-world reporting (Yossi Gozlan: 'The Hawks will use nearly their entire $15 million mid-level exception… His Non Bird rights are too low'; hoopsrumors.com/2026/06/jock-landale-re-signing-with-hawks.html) ⇒ NT-MLE $14.0M consumed, first-apron hard cap. CORRECTED from an earlier own-re-sign misread. Kingston Flemings / Zuby Ejiofor rookie-scale; Henri Veesaar 2nd-round exception; C.J. McCollum extension.

BKN.rationale: Own re-signs (Jun 29, options declined then re-signed — Bird family, consume nothing): Day'Ron Sharpe 2y/$20M (y1 9,756,098), Josh Minott 2y/$9M (y1 4,390,244). Outside deals: Keon Ellis (prior CLE) 2y/$18M y1 8,780,488 (Jun 30); Moritz Wagner (prior ORL) 2y/$19M y1 9,268,293 (Jul 1). Both exceed the TP-MLE and cannot share one NT-MLE (aggregate 18,048,781 > 15,044,000) ⇒ room team. But room alone can't cover both either: post-re-sign base = 171,142,688 committed − 18,048,781 = 153,093,907, leaving max 11,867,093 of room even with every hold renounced. The only arithmetic that closes: Ellis signed into cap room, Wagner via the Room MLE — 9,268,293 of 9,366,000, $97,707 under the full Room MLE (just outside the ±60k heuristic, but the signing order Jun 30 → Jul 1 and the room math both support it). Forced renounced: keepable holds ≤ 164,961,000 − 153,093,907 − 8,780,488 = 3,086,605 vs 75,481,187 of current holds ⇒ shed ≥ 72,394,582; minimal largest-holds set is the 12 listed (keeps only Grant Nelson's 2,449,421). Ambiguity: any ONE of the three ~2.45M holds (tre scott / malachi smith / grant nelson) could be the survivor, or all 13 were renounced; roster charges ignored. Two-ways skipped (Chaney Johnson QO, Tyler Bilodeau); Mikel Brown Jr. rookie scale. Room/Room-MLE usage triggers no apron hard cap. RESOLVED (Jul 6): the ~$25M-reported vs ~$3M-computed room discrepancy was a reconciliation miss, not a renounce ambiguity — Nic Claxton's $23.1M stayed on BKN's sheet after the Jun 22 three-teamer because the trade prose says 'Nicolas' (name-variant fallback added; Claxton now on CHI). BKN room recomputes to ~$26M, matching reporting.

BOS.rationale: Mitchell Robinson (prior NYK) 3y/$47.3886M: y1 = 15,796,200×3/3.15 = 15,044,000 — the FULL 2026-27 Non-Taxpayer MLE to the exact dollar; decisive NT-MLE usage → first-apron hard cap. Mike Conley (prior MIN) 1y/3,876,529 = vet-min scale top exactly → minimum exception, consumes nothing. Ron Harper Jr.: BOS declined his $2.58M option then re-signed 3y/$8.99M (y1 2,853,551) — own re-sign AND min-sized, consumes nothing. Amari Williams two-way (skip); Chris Cenac Jr. rookie scale; Neemias Queta extension. BOS committed ~$198.2M — over the cap but under the first apron, consistent with full NT-MLE use. OFFICIAL (Jul 6): Ron Harper Jr. upgraded to 4y/$13,548,235 (y1 3,150,752) — fits Non-Bird 120%-of-minimum (4-YOS min 2,667,947 x 1.2 = 3,201,536), consumes no exception; booked via a curated sheet stub since he had no 2025-26 NBA contract row.

CHA.rationale: Coby White 3y/$74M (y1 = 24,666,667×3/3.15 = 23,492,064): OWN re-sign — in this world's base data his 2025-26 team is CHA (contracts-2025-26.json, $12,888,889) — Bird, consumes nothing at any amount. No other CHA feed signings and no trade rows involving him (not an S&T). CHA committed ~$167.1M post-re-sign, a routine over-cap Bird outcome; no exception use, no hard cap.

CHI.rationale: Norman Powell (prior MIA) 2y/$45M: y1 = 22,500,000×2/2.05 = 21,951,220 > NT-MLE (15,044,000) ⇒ must be a cap-room signing → operatedUnderCap, NT/TP-MLE+BAE dead for the year; no trade row for Powell, so not an S&T. Room math: committed 142,783,119 − 21,951,220 = 120,831,899 pre-spree base; keepable holds ≤ 164,961,000 − 120,831,899 − 21,951,220 = 22,177,881 vs 35,303,610 current holds ⇒ must shed ≥ 13,125,729. Largest-hold solution: Jaden Ivey (19,203,610) alone, leaving Richards+Yabusele (16,100,000) intact ≤ 22.18M. Ambiguity: renouncing Richards (9.5M) + Yabusele (6.6M) and keeping Ivey also balances — hence medium confidence, Ivey listed per the prefer-largest rule. Zach Collins is an extension; Caleb Wilson / Dailyn Swain rookie scale; Sellers/Awaka two-way. Post-feed CHI sits ~$142.8M, under the cap — consistent with a room team; no Room MLE signing observed (nothing near 9,366,000) and no hard cap.

CLE.rationale: Thomas Bryant 1y/3,524,948: OWN re-sign (prior CLE) and also minimum-sized (3,524,948 ≤ 3,916,529) — consumes nothing on both grounds. Meleek Thomas = 2nd-round exception; Ernest Udeh Jr. two-way (skip). Keon Ellis LEAVING (prior CLE → BKN) only clears a CLE hold, no CLE consumption. CLE committed ~$185.9M — over-cap team with no MLE/BAE use and no in-world hard cap. Aug 19: Cleveland ACQUIRED Peyton Watson (4y/$88M, y1 20,465,116 at 5% raises — our y1 and y4 match SI's reported ~$20.5M and $23.5M) by sign-and-trade in the five-team deal, which hard-caps the ACQUIRING team at the first apron ($209,015,000) for the season. Sourced three ways: Hoops Rumors, Keith Smith (Spotrac) and Yossi Gozlan (The Third Apron) all put Cleveland's post-trade room at $28.4M under that cap, and our pre-Harden sheet reads $180,603,872 — $28,411,128 of room, the reported figure to the dollar. The S&T consumes no Cleveland exception (Denver signed him on Bird rights); the hard cap is the whole cost. Aug 20: Harden re-signed 3y/$97M, y1 booked 29,938,272 at the 8% Bird raise, which Gozlan independently describes as 'a max starting salary just shy of $30 million.' That is $1,527,144 MORE than the room, and the overage is REAL, not a reconciliation error — Gozlan names the clearing route in the same breath: 'They could also stretch Cam Whitmore for a little more flexibility.' Stretching Whitmore's $5,458,000 over three years charges $1,819,333 and frees $3,638,667, which fits Harden and leaves ~$2.1M for a 15th man. Until the feed carries that waive, Cleveland sits over its own hard cap with an agreed-but-unfiled contract — see the documented exception in feedState.test.ts.

DAL.rationale: No feed FA signings for DAL in signings.json (only trades: Aldama/Biberovic in from MEM Jul 1, Sergio de Larrea in via 4-team deal Jun 24 — trades, not exception signings). No MLE/BAE usage, no S&T acquisition, no hard cap triggered by feed moves.

DEN.rationale: Tyus Jones 1yr $3,876,529 (y1 = min scale top exactly, prior DAL) — minimum exception, consumes nothing. Marvin Bagley III 1yr $3,506,659 (y1 below min top, prior DAL) — minimum exception, consumes nothing. No exception usage, no hard cap.

DET.rationale: John Collins 3yr/$51M (y1 16,190,476, prior LAC) — VERIFIED sign-and-trade: Jul 1 transaction reads 'contract with LA Clippers (LAC) as part of a sign-and-trade with Detroit (DET)' (same pattern as Kessler UTA→LAL); DET is the acquirer ⇒ hard-capped at first apron, consumes no MLE. Kevin Huerter 3yr/$27M (y1 8,571,429) — prior team DET in contracts-2025-26 (25-26 salary $17.99M) ⇒ own re-sign, Bird family, consumes nothing. Javonte Green 1yr $3,943,679 — prior team DET ⇒ own re-sign (y1 is $27,150 over the min+40k line, but Bird/Early Bird covers it: 175% of his $2,296,274 = $4,018,480), consumes nothing. Only cap consequence: first-apron hard cap from the Collins S&T acquisition.

GSW.rationale: Al Horford 2yr/$13,985,100 (y1 = 6,822,000, prior GSW, declined $5.97M PO) — y1 is EXACTLY 120% of his $5,685,000 prior salary ⇒ Non-Bird own re-sign, consumes nothing. De'Anthony Melton (prior GSW, declined $3.45M PO) is the TAXPAYER MID-LEVEL, per Bobby Marks (Jul 28, replying on the Draymond re-signing): "Green signing for less would not have opened up more than the $6.1M tax ML. The tax ML is designated to De'Anthony Melton." ⇒ SECOND-apron hard cap. UPDATED Aug 6: the deal came in at the FULL exception — 2yr/$12,431,200, y1 = $6,064,000, which is the 2026-27 taxpayer MLE to the dollar, with the 5% raise on top. It was carried at 2yr/$11,227,850 (y1 $5,477,000) while it was still reported terms, which left a phantom $587,000 of the exception on Golden State's sheet after the real contract had already spent all of it — the kind of error that only shows up as an offer the team cannot actually make. Nothing remains. Draymond Green re-signed 1yr/$27,678,571 on Jul 28 via BIRD rights — the same figure he opted out of — which is why Golden State can sit ~$213.5M, above the first apron, and still be legal. CORRECTION (Jul 28): an earlier audit read Melton's y1 landing on the Bi-Annual Exception to the dollar ($5,477,000 = the 2026-27 BAE exactly) as proof the BAE was spent, and pinned a FIRST-apron cap. That coincidence was a trap: the Draymond re-signing cleared the first apron, which a first-apron hard cap makes impossible, and Marks names the taxpayer MLE outright. Reporting had also described a planned BAE-for-Melton / NT-MLE-for-LeBron structure — that plan died with the LeBron pursuit, and Golden State pivoted to Bird rights for Green plus the taxpayer MLE for Melton. Marks' "$8.3M below the 2nd apron" framing is exactly the live constraint this cap creates.

HOU.rationale: Tari Eason 5yr/$81.5M (y1 14,818,182, prior HOU, RFA off HOU qualifying offer) — own re-sign, Bird, consumes nothing. Marcus Smart 2yr with a year-2 player option (prior LAL — declined $5.39M PO): Hoops Rumors (Jul 1) is explicit — Houston wanted three years but that “would need … the non-taxpayer mid-level exception … a hard cap at the first tax apron,” so the team “is instead poised to add Smart using the taxpayer mid-level exception, resulting in a second-apron hard cap instead,” and “a two-year taxpayer MLE deal technically caps out at about $12.43MM” vs Charania’s rounded $13MM. Booked at the FULL TP-MLE: y1 = 6,064,000 exactly, y2 (PO) = 6,367,200, total $12,431,200 — the earlier 6,368,000/$13,054,400 was the same source-estimate rounding as Kennard’s (PHX). TP-MLE use ⇒ hard-capped at the SECOND apron, not the first. Bogdan Bogdanovic 1yr $3,876,529 (y1 = min scale top exactly, prior LAC — option declined) — minimum exception, consumes nothing. Not near Room MLE; no under-cap inference.

IND.rationale: Kelly Oubre Jr. 2yr/$16.5M OFFICIAL (Spotrac; y1 = 8,048,780 with the standard 5% raise — the “$17M” headline was rounded; prior PHI) — outside deal; above TP-MLE, not within ±$60k of Room MLE ($9,366,000), fits under NT-MLE ⇒ partial NT-MLE ⇒ hard-capped at first apron. Hoops Rumors (Jul 1) confirms both the mechanism (“a portion of their non-taxpayer mid-level exception”) and the cap state (“just $1.6MM below a first-apron hard cap with 14 players under contract” — our reconciled sheet shows the same 14 players $1.60M below). Jul 8: Micah Potter’s non-guaranteed $2.8M was waived to ZERO dead money (Hoops Rumors), and Larry Nance Jr.’s agreed vet-min is held as PENDING — the ~$2.45M charge would sit ~$0.85M over this very hard cap on our sheet and his guarantee structure is unresolved (see roster-corrections-2026.json pendingSignings).

LAC.rationale: Jordan Miller 3y/$15.3M (y1=$4,857,143; prior LAC, option declined then QO'd — Bird re-sign, consumes nothing). Kobe Sanders 4y/$11.2M (y1=$2,604,651; prior LAC RFA, and minimum-sized anyway — consumes nothing). John Collins (prior LAC, $26.58M 2025-26): signed 3y/$51M (y1=$16,190,476) with LAC via Bird as part of a sign-and-trade to DET — the ACQUIRER (DET) is hard-capped at the first apron, not LAC; the outgoing S&T consumes no LAC exception. Committed $147.2M (over cap), no exception usage, no hard cap triggered. Jul 6: Rui Hachimura 2y/$28M (y1 13,658,537, 2027-28 team option) via the mid-level exception — Fischer: 'by way of their mid-level exception, per source'; Gozlan: 'fits in the mid-level exception, which would hard cap them to the first apron' (he notes cap space was the alternative structure; the MLE reporting is sourced, so we book NT-MLE). Aug 13: Bradley Beal 2y/$13,170,840 (y1 6,424,800) is a NON-BIRD re-sign, not mid-level money — year one is 120% of his $5,354,000 Clipper salary to the dollar, which is the Non-Bird ceiling exactly. The attribution matters both ways: it is above the taxpayer MLE ($6,064,000) and the BAE ($5,477,000), and L.A. has only $1,385,463 of NT-MLE left after Hachimura, so no exception on their books could have paid it. Consumes nothing; the Hachimura first-apron hard cap is untouched at $169.6M committed. Jalen Pickett (Aug 12) is a two-way.

LAL.rationale: Reaves 4y/$184.76M max (y1=$42,966,586; prior LAL, declined PO — Bird, consumes nothing). Kessler 4y/$130M (y1=$30,232,558) acquired via UTA sign-and-trade for picks only — no matching salary, absorbed into room; S&T acquisition hard-caps LAL at the first apron regardless. Outside deals: Grimes (prior PHI) y1=$13,953,488 and Mamukelashvili (prior TOR) y1=$12,093,023 — two NT-MLE-sized deals cannot share the one NT-MLE, and aggregate $35.4M (plus unmatched Kessler $30.2M) far exceeds NT-MLE+BAE ($20.5M), so LAL demonstrably operated under the cap (room signings; NT/TP-MLE+BAE dead per Art. VII 6(n)(1)/6(g)(3)). Sexton (prior CHI) y1=$9,366,000.00 — EXACTLY the Room MLE to the dollar, confirming room operation. Renounce math: pre-spree base $86,674,513; room used $56,279,069; max room with zero holds $78,286,487 leaves only $22.0M slack, and Reaves' retained Bird hold (~$20.9–26.5M at 150–190% of $13,937,574) plus incomplete-roster charges consumes it all — so LeBron James ($57,736,350), Rui Hachimura ($27,388,889), and Maxi Kleber ($20,900,000) holds are all mathematically incompatible and must be renounced. Ambiguity: at a 190% Reaves hold the sequence is ~$4.5M short even fully renounced (resolvable via ordering/hold treatment), hence medium confidence; the three listed renouncements are required under every ordering.

MEM.rationale: No 2026 offseason feed signings for MEM (committed $139.0M; FA holds Niang/Gordon et al. untouched). Nothing consumed, no hard cap.

Simone Fontecchio 1y/$2.63M (y1=$2,625,627; prior MIA and minimum-sized — consumes nothing). MIA's $203.5M sits under the projected first apron, consistent.

MIN.rationale: Ayo Dosunmu 5y/$112M (y1=$20,363,636): prior team is MIN per contracts-2025-26 (in-world, not CHI) ⇒ own re-sign via Bird, any amount, consumes nothing — NOT a room signing despite y1 > NT-MLE. Jaylen Clark 3y/$10M (y1=$3,174,603; prior MIN RFA and minimum-sized). Bones/Nah'Shon Hyland 1y/$2.85M (prior MIN, minimum-sized). Enrique Freeman two-way (skipped). Ariel Hukporti 1yr y1 3,400,000 (prior NYK) fits the minimum exception (≤ 3,916,529), consumes nothing. Rayan Rupert is a Two-Way per transactions; Caleb Love appears in signings.json as PHI but transactions show him agreeing to a Two-Way with POR — either way two-way/min-marker, skipped. Not a room team (NT-MLE use precludes it), so no forced renouncements of Lowry/Beauchamp/Watford/Martin holds. OFFICIAL (Jul 6 filings): Dean Wade 4y/$38.7M y1 9,000,000 + Anfernee Simons 2y/$12.3M y1 6,000,000 = exactly 15,000,000 of the 15,044,000 NT-MLE — $44,000 technically unused (below any signable salary). First-apron hard cap unchanged.

PHX.rationale: Collin Gillespie 4/48M y1 11,162,791, Mark Williams 3/38M y1 12,063,492 (RFA, QO tendered), Jordan Goodwin 3/19M y1 6,031,746 — all prior team PHX, own re-signs via Bird rights, consume nothing (and confirm PHX operated over the cap). Booked at the FULL TP-MLE: y1 = 6,064,000 exactly, y2 (PO) = 6,367,200, total $12,431,200 — the “$13M” headline and the earlier 6,368,000/$13,054,400 estimate were the source rounding hot. VII 3(f) charges at the 2-YOS figure of $2,449,421 — the point of the exercise for a team under a second-apron hard cap. Minimum exception, consumes nothing. Dillon Brooks' 3y/$73M extension (Aug 5, official Aug 8) starts in 2027-28 and does not touch the 2026-27 sheet.

Alijah Martin 2yr/$4,757,011 (y1 = 2,320,493 <= min top; own two-way RFA) -> minimum. Hepburn and Bradley two-ways skipped; Graves rookie scale. Kawhi arrived by trade. UTA.rationale: Jusuf Nurkic 2yr/$22M (y1 = 10,731,707): prior team UTA -> own Bird re-sign, consumes nothing. Walker Kessler 4yr/$130M is a sign-and-trade OUT (UTA signs via Bird and sends to LAL): hard-caps the acquirer LAL, not UTA, and consumes no UTA exception. Trey Alexander/Bates two-ways skipped. Okogie exceeds the BAE (5,477,000) by $377k, so TP-MLE(Hayes)+BAE(Okogie) is incoherent; the only coherent over-cap attribution is the NT-MLE split across both players (6,064,000 + 5,853,659 = 11,917,659 <= 15,044,000; the NT-MLE is a splittable aggregate under CBA Art. VII 6(e)) -> first-apron hard cap. Confidence medium because Hayes's y1 is exactly TP-MLE-sized, suggesting the feed may have intended TP-MLE (which would imply a second-apron hard cap and leave Okogie unexplained).

WAS.rationale: Trae Young 4yr/$212,799,690 (y1 = 49,488,300): prior team WAS per contracts-2025-26 ($46.39M) and he declined a $48.97M WAS player option on Jun 17 -> own Bird (max) re-sign, consumes nothing at any amount. Jul 8 2026: acquired Khris Middleton (3yr/$17.61M, signed by DAL) via the 6-team sign-and-trade, sending out D'Angelo Russell + 2nd-round picks — WAS is the sign-and-trade ACQUIRER, so it is hard-capped at the first apron ($209.015M) for the season (Art. VII). That is the only new cap consequence.
